rites.name: Zephiasora
rites.text: Zephiasora is a concept of the Lyemwen Arcane Realm, born in the Fall of the Second Age when the Sundering broke the old worlds into Shards. It is the sworn vow that held the groves and young kingdoms together during the reign of the first sovereign.

rites.name: Siluanneth
rites.text: Siluanneth is the concept of the Lyemwen tide that drew breath from the Sundering, a binding thread woven through the Shards and the oath of the Pact. Its devotees in the Holy Age kindled flame in its name and raised temples where the broken worlds were remembered. It is known less as a force than as the promise that fragments might one day be mended.

rites.name: Corasor
rites.text: Corasor is the concept of the bonding-current that held the Lyemwen worlds together until the Fall, when its threads were cut and drawn into the Shards. Within the Age of Sundering it became the oath-bond by which surviving peoples recall what the Pact cost them. It is remembered less as a force than as a debt owed across broken skies.

rites.name: Nintium
rites.text: Nintium is a concept in the Arcane Realm of Lyemwen, born in the Fall and bound into the Pact sworn after the Sundering. It is said to hold the memory of broken worlds, flaring whenever landfall tears an old bond apart in the Age of Sundering.

rites.name: Osiasith
rites.text: Osiasith is the concept of the walled wardens of Lyemwen, the quiet discipline that keeps the holding walls standing through the Walled Age. It is embodied in the lamplit orders and the first crossings that tested the stones against the dark beyond. It binds people to keep a promise made to the stones.

rites.name: Ilyalys
rites.text: Ilyalys is a sealed sigil-technique of the Lyemwen arcane orders, named for the astral weaver who first bent void-threads into a grasping hand. Practitioners conjure a shimmering construct of condensed starlight that can seize, batter, or interpose itself as a barrier against incoming force.

rites.name: Venaerlys
rites.text: Venaerlys is a gentle enchantment woven into the fabric of Lyemwen's fourth-age sorcery, binding a target's breath to a helpless, rolling mirth that leaves them unable to act. Its wielders treat it as a mercy-spell for disarming duels and calming frightened crowds, though the old mages whisper that its true reach has never been measured.

rites.name: Ryilora
rites.text: Ryilora is a concept of pure arcane sovereignty in Lyemwen, a principle that gathers into the will of whoever dares to name it aloud. Its scholars claim that every working drawn from it leaves a faint signature, a hum that lingers in the ley-lines for three ages after the caster has gone to dust.

rites.name: Bronar
rites.text: Bronar is the concept of the Branching Hour in Lyemwen's Arcane Realm, the moment in the seventh Era when a single ending splits into the Three Futures. It is pictured as a standing door that the Library catalogues rather than opens, so every outcome is shelved and none is chosen.

rites.name: Karaigun
rites.text: Karaigun is a concept held in Lyemwen's Arcane Realm during the Age of the first sovereign, when groves and kingdoms were still growing. It names the pull that bends a single branching future toward the one the Library later shelves. Its force is that of a kingdom's binding oath, stored and released once into the grove-roots.
